Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The `revert` method in the `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line` class creates a new `Line` object with the direction negated. The issue seems to be related to precision loss when negating the direction.

Next, I will investigate the `getDirection` method in the `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line` class to understand the precision handling in retrieving the direction.

The `getDirection` method simply returns the direction vector of the line without any additional computations or modifications.

Given that the failing test mentions imprecise calculations with the direction, it's likely that the issue lies in how the direction vector is initially created or stored in the `Line` class. 

I will now retrieve the code snippet for the constructor of the `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line` class to further investigate the precision handling during initialization.

To identify the potential source of precision loss when initializing the direction vector, I will retrieve the code snippet of the `reset` method in the `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line` class.

messages.content:
The `reset` method in the `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line` class calculates the direction vector based on the difference between two points (`p2.subtract(p1)`), normalizes it, and then creates a new `Vector3D` object for the direction.

The issue of imprecise calculations with the direction vector might stem from the normalization step or other calculations involving the direction vector during initialization in the `reset` method.

To address the precision loss in the direction vector initialization, a potential fix could involve improving the precision during normalization or by using more precise calculations when setting up the direction vector in the `reset` method.

The constructor `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line.Line(org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Vector3D,org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Vector3D)` and the method `org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Line.reset(org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Vector3D,org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.Vector3D)` are the best locations to address the precision issues in the direction vector initialization.
